item.title: [ 63] /napt/ AI Pokemon Thread #278: Neon Genesis Edition
item.description:
Previously on /napt/:
>>59599605

This is a general thread for people to post their AI art and/or make requests from others who may want to attempt making their own Pokémon-related gens.

Local Generation is the best option, requires a video card. Guides for local genning can be found in the /g/ threads:
https://rentry.org/comfyui_guide_1girl
>>>/g/ldg
Other Stable Diffusion threads are on: /h/, /e/, /d/, /b/, /vt/, /aco/, /trash/

NovelAI v4.5 is a paid AI generator. Opus tier users have "unlimited" Small/Normal generations, though editing tools require credits.

Midjourney is a paid AI generator, also capable of video. Usage requires a monthly subscription, with basically infinite gens.

Microsoft's Bing AI is a free image generator that is powered by DALL·E 3.

Civitai is free using its ‘buzz’ currency. You get a certain amount every day, plus more for liking models and gens.
>civitai.com

Otaiku is a (mostly) free mobile app. An ad watch is required between each image generation unless you pay.
>ailla.biz/otaiku
free video generation
>videomaker.me/app

Tensor is another generator that gives free daily credits, as well as a vast library of LoRAs to train your prompts on. Subscriptions are available for those who wish to pursue more than this.
>https://tensor.art/

Pastebin of Pokémon artists:
>https://pastebin.com/U0mmK3Tm (embed) (embed)

Characters with under 50 images will require more tags to have them look correct. This is a list of all Pokémon characters with over 300 images:
>https://danbooru.donmai.us/posts?tags=*_%28pokemon%29+&z=5

[Multiple images to share? Conserve space. Either collage or catbox them.]

[NO grotesque or violent images. If you really wanna share those, catbox them.]

>Heya, fellow /napts, I've updated the Novelai artist tool to 4.5, and added an ELO ranking system so you can rank your favorite artists more easily.

item.title: [ 79] /bsg/ - Bank Shutdown General
item.description:
Spinda Edition
Stolen Thumbnail Edition
Previous >>59579559

>What's happening?
Pokemon Bank shuts down on February 25th, 2027.

>What does this mean?
Gens 3 through 5 will forever feature forward migration (from old gen up to >nugen) via Gen 4 Pal Park and Gen 5 Poké Transfer Lab.
Gens 6 & Gen 7 will be permanently locked out of all transfers. That means no transferring Gen 5 to 6, no Gen 6 to 7, no Gen 7 to Home.
Virtual Console releases of Gens 1 & 2 will be locked to only trading across those titles.
Basically anything that isn't a Switch1/2 title or PokemonGO will be unable to transfer to Home.

>What can I do about this?
Access to a modded 3DS can expedite the transfer (and procurement) of Pokemon to move into Home before the shutdown via homebrew titles. They can also enable you to continue transferring across Gens 1 through 7 in lieu of Bank. No getting around the Home lockout though.

>What is this thread for?
Discuss things we're trying to get done before Bank closes down. Ribbons are a big one, transferring up old events. Getting Pokemon that can't be obtained in the current generation. The opportunity to transfer up GB origin marks for the gen 1 and 2 VC and origin marks for Kalos and Alola will also disappear unless/until those games/marks are reintroduced on the Switch.

>List of home challenges that will become impossible to complete:

Democrat Adam Hamilton narrowly leads Republican Sen. Roger Marshall in a tight race for Senate in Kansas, according to new polling.

Hamilton, senior pastor of the Church of the Resurrection, is campaigning to become the first Democrat to win a Sunflower State Senate race since former Sen. George McGill in 1932. Marshall is vying for a second term after winning the seat by double digits in 2020.

Former Kansas Gov. Bill Graves (R) backed Hamilton this week, saying the country is “facing increasing partisan gridlock and division” and that it’s “time Kansas does something different.”

A Kansas wacko is behind bars after allegedly threatening to kill conservative podcaster Ben Shapiro, who opened up about daily security concerns in a new interview.

Korby Allen Strube, 29, was arrested recently by Florida police for allegedly posting a spree of vile antisemitic threats on X, including a menacing countdown to Yom Kippur and insinuations something would happen to Shapiro on the Jewish holiday.

“I’m going to kill be Shapiro and hes not gonna be a-live,” read a July 31 post, with a deluge of menace pouring across Strube’s X account over the following days, police records obtained by The Post showed.

“I’ll kill you just the same. Go meet Jesus. 51 days left,” read another. “Die with Jesus … I’ll kill you just the same I guess. 52 days.”

Others claimed Shapiro would be killed “for being Jewish,” or else called him a “stupid jew,” with police determining the countdown to the supposed murder plot coincided with this year’s Yom Kippur dates.

The threats weren’t just reserved for Shapiro – Strube allegedly named President Trump, the Obamas and suggested his social media behavior had somehow led to the death of Shapiro’s fellow conservative commentator Charlie Kirk.

The posts were flagged to police by a security firm hired by Shapiro – who said the threats were “not veiled” and had a “level of gravity.”

Officials quickly tracked the X account to an address near Topeka, where Strube was found living with his parents.

Strube owned up to making the posts, police alleged, before launching a disturbed tale about government spies who were sending him messages through song lyrics and presidential addresses.

Texas Democrats have allegedly found a “roundabout” way to pay for votes in the critical Senate and governor’s races, according to an undercover video published Wednesday.

A Democratic operative with Texas Majority PAC admitted in the new footage released by the conservative outlet Townhall that the group is shelling out $25 per person for attendance at Zoom classes that discuss “bad things” Republicans are doing.

“We are paying people $25 to attend a one-hour Zoom class to learn why voting is important and why the Republicans are causing all of these bad things,” said Sky MacAdams, an organizing manager for Texas Majority PAC.

“So it’s like a roundabout way of paying people for their votes, essentially,” he added, calling the move a bit of a “gray” area.

Federal law prohibits payments in exchange for voting or not voting for certain candidates, with violators potentially facing up to two years in prison.

The paid relational program, as its known, compensates low-propensity voters “for their time as they reach, persuade, and mobilize their friends and family to vote,” according to the website for Relentless, a political consulting firm.

>how to get started
Purchase a corn cob pipe (or a cheap briar pipe) and a pouch of Half and Half or Captain Black tobacco from a smoke shop
or online. You will need a lighter or match, and something to tamp it with--a large nail works well if you don't have a pipe tool.
Fill the pipe with tobacco, pack it down halfway, top it off, pack it down to 3/4, top it off again, pack gently and enjoy. Smoke
slower than you think you need to, the tobacco tastes best when it is burning cool. Tamp and re-light as needed. If you still
have trouble, try different methods on YouTube until you find one that works for you.
>smoking a pipe will give you cancer
Originally the Surgeon General found that pipe and cigar smokers, following a careful study of the statistics (at a time when
most adults smoked, so they had a good sample size), had insignificant death rate increases. Nowadays, tobacco is being
legislated against while hard drugs are being legalized. Put two and two together. Tobacco is just another good thing under attack by the government.
